tabs.title: Pattern A: four notes
tabs.note: Hold the named chord. Let notes overlap naturally. Small F is xx3211; its top two strings share an index-finger barre.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Pinch on beat 1
tabs.rhythm: 4/4 · bass and treble together, then three single notes
tabs.note: Start both notes together on beat 1. If the attacks split, slow down and prepare thumb and ring finger on the strings.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Pattern B: eight notes
tabs.note: Say 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. The metronome clicks only on the numbered beats.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: C–Am: land on beat 1
tabs.note: Let the bass ring while you prepare the next shape. After two bars, return to C. Add full picking only when these landings are steady.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Happy Birthday: melody in C
tabs.rhythm: 3/4 · first two notes are pickup eighths on 3 &
tabs.tempo: Slow enough to hum and play the phrase
tabs.note: This is our own simple melody fingering, not the teacher’s full arrangement. Count 1 2 3. Each phrase starts with two pickup notes on 3 &; the next three notes take one beat each. Hold the last note of phrases 1 and 2 for beats 1–2, then start the next pickup on 3 &. In phrase 3, B and A fall on 1 and 2. Hold the final C for all three beats. In Week 1, learn only a few melody notes; add bass from the lesson when ready.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Alternating bass: thumb only
tabs.note: Hold the chord and keep fingers still. The C second bass note is E, so this is a root/third exercise. Keep D thumb-only until you learn different treble routing.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: A steady root under a small melody
tabs.tempo: Start slower than 60 BPM if needed
tabs.note: An original Am drill: thumb plays every subdivision, while treble notes occur on the numbered beats. Keep melody louder than bass. First play bass alone.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Travis texture: p i p m
tabs.tempo: Start at 40–50 BPM; steady before faster
tabs.note: Hold C. Beat 1 adds a pinch; all later bass attacks remain on the beat. Learn thumb alone, then add one treble attack at a time.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: A four-note melody with sparse bass
tabs.note: Original mini-etude in C. Learn the top line E–C–B–G alone. Then add only the low C on beat 1. Keep the top note audible; this is a layering example, not a published song arrangement.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Bass on 1/3, slap on 2/4
tabs.rhythm: 4/4 · x marks a light muted attack
tabs.note: Hold C. Pluck bass notes normally. On x, make a light percussive contact across the indicated strings; no fret is pressed for the x itself. Practise the movement slowly with the teacher’s video.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Natural harmonics: 12, 7, 5
tabs.note: Angle brackets mean a light touch directly above the fret wire, not a fretted note. Pluck, then lift the touching finger. Start with fret 12; use the video for the hand position.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: One hammer-on over alternating bass
tabs.note: Original Am exercise. Pluck open string 3 on beat 1 with the bass. On the following &, hammer to fret 2 without another picking-hand attack (h). Continue the bass on beats 2, 3 and 4.
tabs.tuning: Standard · E A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Drop-D D-chord arpeggio
tabs.note: Lower only string 6 from E to D with a tuner. Hold xx0232 on strings 4–1. In this example the thumb uses the newly tuned open string 6. Retune before playing standard-tuning examples.
tabs.tuning: Drop D · D A D G B E
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

tabs.title: Open-D arpeggio
tabs.note: Use a tuner for all six strings; the notes are shown thickest to thinnest. This original open-string exercise explores the tuning. It is not the 奇跡の山 score. Return to standard tuning for your standard-tuning studies.
tabs.tuning: Open D · D A D F♯ A D
tabs.credit: Original practice example for this plan

legend: Top line is string 1 (thin high E); bottom line is string 6 (thick low E). Numbers are frets, 0 is open, and notes in the same column sound together. A dash means no new attack, not automatically a rest. p = thumb, i = index, m = middle, a = ring; x = muted percussion, h = hammer-on, and <12> = a natural harmonic. Columns show attack order; use the Count row and rhythm instructions for timing.
